title: Edge evidence gateway & transformer — design notes
content:
Purpose:

This is a working design and run-notes document for the proposed Edge Evidence Gateway + Transformer (EEGT). The gateway sits between collectors/agents and downstream evidence sinks (SIEM, archival store, audit index). Goal: provide a compact, secure, observable ingress path that normalizes audit records across sources, enforces RBAC v2 visibility at the ingest/route decision point, applies enrichment and TTL policies, and provides robust backpressure/failover semantics so production services don't lose control-plane evidence when downstream systems are slow.

Scope / non-goals:
- In-scope: schema normalization, per-customer routing, short-term persistence for replay, enrichment (identity/team lookup, token-scoping), rate-limited SIEM exports, basic deduplication, signed evidence envelopes, replay from archive.
- Out-of-scope (for this doc): long-term archival policies, SIEM parsing rules beyond mapping to ECS-like JSON, deep forensic chain-of-custody UI (that is separate but will pull from the gateway archival store).

High-level architecture (sketch):

  1) Edge Collector / Agent -> HTTPS -> Edge Evidence Gateway (EEGT) ingress endpoint
     - TLS mutual optional for on-prem; HMAC + request-signature for hosted collectors
  2) Ingress -> lightweight request validation & rate enforcement -> enqueue into per-tenant priority queue
  3) Transformer worker pool consumes from queues, performs schema mapping -> enrichment -> attaches metadata (policy_id, retention_tier, rbac_visibility) -> produces an "evidence envelope"
  4) Router: decisions to (a) forward to SIEM exporter over gRPC/HTTPS (real-time), (b) write to short-term durable queue for replay (S3/MinIO) and asynchronous export, or (c) drop/archive based on TTL/cost rules
  5) Export adapters: SIEM exporter(s) (ECS JSON or CEF syslog adapter), internal audit-index writer, archival writer
  6) Control plane: admin API for RBAC v2 visibility rules, routing policies, and tenant configs

State machine for an evidence envelope (recommended minimal states):

  - RECEIVED (ingress accepted, assigned request_id)
  - VALIDATED (schema + signature ok)
  - NORMALIZED (mapped to canonical audit schema)
  - ENRICHED (identity/team lookups, token metadata)
  - ROUTED (export attempted)
  - ACKED (target acknowledged) OR QUEUED_FOR_REPLAY OR FAILED
  - ARCHIVED (written to durable store)
  - RETIRED (aged out per retention policy)

Transitions and retry semantics:
- VALIDATED -> NORMALIZED: immediate; if schema mismatch -> route to "quarantine" bucket with sampled copy and alert (do not block other events).
- ROUTED -> ACKED: for SIEM synchronous export, use at-least-once semantics with idempotency keys (request_id). Retries use exponential backoff up to N attempts, then move to QUEUED_FOR_REPLAY.
- QUEUED_FOR_REPLAY: durable queue + metadata to re-run transformation if mapping rules changed later.

Canonical audit schema (minimum fields, used by downstream controls & RBAC v2):
- envelope_id: UUID v4 (string)
- request_id: string (upstream request id if present)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- source: {source_type, collector_id}  -- flattened to source_type, collector_id in canonical shape
- actor.id, actor.type, actor.principal_name
- actor.roles: list of role ids (used by RBAC v2 visibility)
- action: string (verb-like, e.g., token.create, model.deploy)
- resource.type, resource.id, resource.owner_team
- outcome: success | failure | unknown
- client.ip, user_agent
- trace_id, span_id (if present)
- raw_payload_hash: sha256
- retention_tier: short|medium|long
- rbac_visibility: list (allowed_viewer_roles OR explicit tenant ids)
- signature: base64 (HMAC or asymmetric)

Note: the canonical shape must be extensible (free-form metadata map) but the fields above are indexed in audit-index. All keys are strings; arrays are arrays of strings.

Schema mapping rules / examples (quick picks):
- Kubernetes audit: map verb -> action, user.username -> actor.principal_name, user.groups -> actor.roles, objectRef.resource -> resource.type, namespace/name -> resource.id
- Redwood API access logs: request.user_id -> actor.id, request.scopes -> actor.roles, route -> action, modelId -> resource.id

Enrichment patterns (cheap, cache-heavy):
- Identity lookup: resolve actor.id -> {team, manager, employment_status} from identity service cache (TTL 5m)
- Role expansion: map role ids to RBAC v2 role objects (for visibility); cache policy decisions in memory for 30s
- Geo/IP: bulk enrichment using local geodb with async fallback to remote provider
- Token scoping: lookup token metadata to surface "is_machine_token" and token_owner_team

Backpressure & flow control strategy:
1) Per-tenant token-bucket quota at ingress for request rate control
2) Per-tenant and per-target queue depth thresholds; when thresholds exceeded:
   - Soft threshold: mark events as low-priority, switch transformer to sampling mode (only enrich high-priority events), emit metrics/alerts
   - Hard threshold: circuit-break export to SIEM and route all new events to ARCHIVE WITH METADATA for later replay, persist reason code: BACKPRESSURE_EXPORT_UNAVAILABLE
3) Queue persistence: short-term durable queue on fast object store (S3/MinIO) with manifest files to avoid per-object overhead
4) Offramp: when downstream (SIEM) recovers, background replays will restore delivery order (best-effort). Use idempotency keys to avoid duplicates.

Deduplication and idempotency:
- Primary dedupe key: raw_payload_hash + source.timestamp (plus collector_id).
- Maintain small bloom filter / LRU cache for recent IDs; for long-duplicates rely on SIEM idempotency where supported.

RBAC v2 considerations (ingest-time enforcement):
- The gateway will compute rbac_visibility for each envelope based on actor.roles and resource.owner_team using rules from Control Plane. That visibility is stored on the envelope and used by downstream indexers and query gates to enforce who can view evidence.
- Admin operations (muting, quarantining, replays) require explicit admin RBAC scopes and use the same v2 policy engine for authorization.
- Audit trail: every decision (why an event was archived, why replayed) must itself be written as an audit event with its own envelope and retention.

Security & signing model:
- Ingress: collectors sign payloads with HMAC-SHA256 using per-collector key; gateway verifies before accepting.
- Internal service-to-service: mTLS + JWTs minted by control plane.
- Envelopes persisted in archive are encrypted at rest with tenant-specific KMS keys where required (Private deployments).
- Access to the gateway admin APIs require RBAC v2 scope: evidence.gateway.admin

SIEM export format mapping (recommended):
- Primary sink: ECS-like JSON mapping (field names chosen above) delivered over HTTPS to SIEM connector. Falls back to syslog (CEF) via adapter if required.
- Minimal transport contract: envelope_id, timestamp, actor.*, action, resource.*, outcome, client.ip, trace_id, raw_payload_hash, rbac_visibility.
- Include a small "gateway_metadata" object with forwarder_version, transform_rules_sha, and route_decision. This helps compliance teams validate what transform rules were applied.

Operational runbook snippets (triage patterns):
- "High queue depth for tenant X"
  1) Check metrics: ingress_rate, transform_latency, downstream_ack_rate for tenant X.
  2) Confirm downstream health: SIEM endpoint 5xx rate.
  3) If downstream is saturated, manually toggle route to ARCHIVE for tenant X and annotate reason.
  4) Kick off replay job when SIEM stable.

- "Schema mismatch quarantine alert"
  1) Pull sample from quarantine bucket, inspect raw_payload and mapped output.
  2) If missing fields are due to collector version drift, notify agents team (ticket template in Confluence).
  3) If this is new action surface, coordinate with product/security to update mapping rules.

Metrics & dashboards (suggested):
- Ingress: requests/sec (per-tenant), invalid_signatures/sec, validated/sec
- Transformer: normalized/sec, enrich_latency_p50/p95/p99, enrichment_cache_hit_ratio
- Routing: routed_to_siem/sec, archived/sec, replay_backlog_size
- Errors: export_failures/sec, quarantine_rate, dedupe_hits/sec

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- routed_to_siem_failure_rate > 5% for 5m -> P1
- per-tenant queue depth > 80% of threshold for 10m -> P2
- quarantine_rate increase > 200% vs baseline -> P2

Storage/retention notes:
- Short-term replay store: keep manifests for 90 days; actual payload retention determined by tenant retention_tier.
- For regulated tenants, preserve chain-of-custody metadata and encryption key ids (KMS key used) in envelope.

Testing & QA checklist (initial rollout):
- Unit tests for every schema mapping rule and transform script
- End-to-end tests with seeded sample events from each collector type (k8s, api-access, infra, audit-logs)
- Chaos test: kill SIEM exporter, confirm route to archive and later replay works
- Load test: push high cardinality of tenants and confirm backpressure behaviors

Backward compatibility / migration path:
- When changing canonical schema, support versioned envelopes (envelope_v1, envelope_v2) and keep transform rules SHA in gateway_metadata so audit-index can reindex older envelopes later.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who ultimately owns the transform rule repository? (security vs infra vs product). Proposal: keep it under security-and-compliance with gate PRs from owning teams.
- Exact RBAC v2 policy language for ingest-time visibility (policy engine evaluation speed constraints). Need microbenchmarking to ensure we can evaluate per-event without adding >1ms median latency.
- Export adapters: implement ECS JSON first, CEF/LEEF later. Which SIEM vendors must be supported in MVP? (ask CS).
- For Private deployments, local KMS integration patterns need confirmation for offline HSM signing.

Notes to self / rough checklist before sharing with wider team:
- Draft swagger for admin API (include route toggles)
- Prototype per-tenant queue manifest format (small JSON list linking to objects)
- Create JIRA EPIC: SIEM-EDGE-GW with sub tasks for transformer, router, archive adapter
- Schedule sync with SRE to design SLOs and alert plumbing

Appendix: sample envelope JSON (flattened sample shown for reviewers)

  "envelope_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "request_id": "req-2024-09-12-xyz",
  "timestamp": "2024-09-12T14:02:03Z",

  "collector_id": "k8s-cluster-prod-3",
  "actor.id": "user:alice@example.com",
  "actor.roles": ["infra-admin", "ci-runner"],

  "resource.id": "default/nginx-1234",
  "outcome": "success",
  "client.ip": "10.2.3.4",
